content: Enalapril belongs to a class of drugs known as angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors. It works by reducing the levels of certain chemicals in the body that cause blood vessels to constrict, thereby allowing blood to flow more easily. Hydrochlorothiazide, on the other hand, is classified as a diuretic, commonly referred to as a water pill. It helps the kidneys eliminate excess water and salt from the body through urine. This medication is available in tablet form and is taken orally, typically once or twice daily, with or without food. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. It is crucial to take the medication exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. If you have questions about additional uses, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Before starting enalapril and hydrochlorothiazide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to enalapril, hydrochlorothiazide, or any related medications, including other ACE inhibitors or sulfa drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Certain drugs, such as NSAIDs, diuretics, diabetes medications, lithium, steroids, and potassium supplements, may interact with this medication, requiring dose adjustments or close monitoring. Inform your doctor if you have a history of heart, liver, kidney, or parathyroid disease; lupus; diabetes; asthma; gout; or angioedema (a condition characterized by swelling, hives, and difficulty breathing). Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking this medication. Alcohol consumption should be discussed with your doctor, as it may exacerbate side effects. If your doctor has recommended a low-sodium or low-salt diet, follow these instructions carefully. Avoid using potassium-containing salt substitutes without consulting your doctor. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. This medication may cause side effects. Common side effects include cough, dizziness, headache, fatigue, muscle cramps, and reduced sexual ability. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, though rare, require immediate medical attention. These include lightheadedness, swelling of the face, throat, tongue, or extremities, hoarseness, difficulty breathing or swallowing, signs of infection (e.g., fever, sore throat, chills), yellowing of the skin or eyes, dry mouth, excessive thirst, weakness, infrequent urination, nausea, vomiting, fainting, chest pain, or an irregular heartbeat. Report any unusual symptoms to your doctor. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA's MedWatch program. Store this medication in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. Do not share this medication with others. Keep a written record of all medications, supplements, and vitamins you are taking, and bring this list to all medical appointments or in case of emergencies. This combination medication is available under the brand name Vaseretic®.
